# wallix-bastion_authdomain_ldap (Resource)

Provides a LDAP authentication domain resource. It depends on a `wallix-bastion_externalauth_ldap`
resource for the actual directory connection, and adds attribute mapping and optional X.509
certificate-based authentication on top.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wallix-bastion_externalauth_ldap" "corporate" {
  authentication_name = "corporate_ldap"
  host                = "ldap.corporate.local"
  port                = 636
  is_ssl              = true
  ldap_base           = "ou=people,dc=corporate,dc=local"
  cn_attribute        = "uid"
  login_attribute     = "uid"
  timeout             = 10
  is_anonymous_access = true
}

resource "wallix-bastion_authdomain_ldap" "corporate" {
  domain_name          = "corporate.local"
  auth_domain_name     = "corporate.com"
  external_auths       = [wallix-bastion_externalauth_ldap.corporate.authentication_name]
  default_language     = "en"
  default_email_domain = "corporate.com"
  description          = "Corporate LDAP directory"
}
```

### With a Certificate Authority (API v3.12+)

```terraform
resource "wallix-bastion_certificate_authority" "corporate" {
  certificate_authority_name = "corporate-ca"
  ca_type                    = "X509"
  ca_certificate             = file("${path.module}/certs/corporate-ca.pem")
  description                = "Corporate PKI root"
}

resource "wallix-bastion_authdomain_ldap" "corporate_pki" {
  domain_name           = "pki.corporate.local"
  auth_domain_name      = "corporate.com"
  external_auths        = [wallix-bastion_externalauth_ldap.corporate.authentication_name]
  default_language      = "en"
  default_email_domain  = "corporate.com"
  certificate_authority = wallix-bastion_certificate_authority.corporate.certificate_authority_name
  enable_ca             = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `auth_domain_name` (String)
- `default_email_domain` (String)
- `default_language` (String)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Usage Notes

### Relationship to externalauth_ldap

`external_auths` references one or more `wallix-bastion_externalauth_ldap.authentication_name`
values, which hold the actual LDAP connection details (host, port, bind credentials, base DN).
This resource layers attribute mapping and authentication-domain settings (default language,
default email domain) on top.

### default_language

Must be one of `de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `ru`.

### X.509 Attributes Are Optional

`check_x509_san_email`, `pubkey_attribute`, `x509_condition`, and `x509_search_filter` only
matter if you're using certificate/smart-card-based authentication against this domain; omit
them for password-based LDAP authentication.

### Certificate Authority

`certificate_authority` is the `certificate_authority_name` of a
`wallix-bastion_certificate_authority`, case-sensitive; the Bastion refuses a name that doesn't
exist. `enable_ca = true` requires it, which is checked at plan. Removing `certificate_authority`
from the configuration detaches the certificate authority, and removing `enable_ca` disables it.

Both arguments require API v3.12 or later and fail at plan with an older API version. API v3.8
doesn't know them: an update of the domain made with API v3.8 detaches a certificate authority
attached with API v3.12.

The Bastion refuses to delete a certificate authority that a domain references, even with
`enable_ca = false`, and Terraform doesn't update the domain before deleting the certificate
authority when both change in one apply. Detach it from the domain and apply first, then remove
the `wallix-bastion_certificate_authority`.

## Import

LDAP authentication domain can be imported using the domain name, e.g.

```shell
terraform import wallix-bastion_authdomain_ldap.corporate corporate.local
```
